structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E050. The tip is E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535. It is E036 plus a group-2 freeze (LR annealed over 75–90%, frozen for the last 10%) plus a +0.25 true-epoch top-up, for about 238 steps. E050 rebuilt the same commit (3df6233) and read 0.7552 at 5.206 s. So the tip's population mean is about 0.754 on seeds 0–2, and time reproduces to about ±0.02 s.

1. Noise. Rebuilds of one commit spread with an SD of about 0.2 pp on the 3-seed mean (E036: 0.7532/0.7525/0.7497/0.7544; E049: 0.7535/0.7552). Forecast bands for neutral changes need ±0.3 pp. I suspect autotune and cuDNN reselection, plus wgrad atomics. The 3-seed gate at 0.753 is close to a coin flip for any change that costs ≥0.1 pp.

2. The wd results act only through the SGD groups. muon_update renormalizes the filters and applies no wd, so filter wd is inert. The optimum is near ×0.5.

3. An annealed freeze is close to free once the block has had its 32 px training, and its saving is 1.5–2× the block's FLOP share. It skips the BN/GELU backward (memory-bound), the Muon NS, the dgrad into the block and the optimizer traffic. E046 showed about 10 ms per frozen step. Moving the anneal start earlier costs accuracy about linearly (E037). The cascade plus top-up has beaten the dial once (E049). Further dose increases trade at about the dial rate, perhaps slightly better.

4. Steps carry accuracy; early pixels don't. E026 and E033 were free. E040, E041, E031 and E048 cost about the dial rate. The dial runs at about 1.2–1.8 s/pp. Loss-based selection is roughly dial-equivalent, so selection plus a top-up nets close to zero.

5. Changes to the objective or the averaging cost 0.2–0.5 pp (E025, E030, E032, E044). The recipe sits at a tuned local optimum in "how training ends". Boosters keep failing.

6. Architecture cuts in the stem. A strided conv in place of conv+pool removes 3/4 of conv1's positions and the biggest memory-bound tensor in the net. I expect a large time saving (about 6–9%). It also loses max-pool invariance, and airbench-style ablations put that at 0.5–1 pp. At 0.7 pp for 0.4 s, the rate is about 0.6 s/pp, worse than the dial. ReLU in place of GELU: the fused kernels are bytes-bound, so the time gain is modest (about 1.5–3%). The accuracy loss is about 0.1–0.3 pp, so the rate is roughly dial-neutral.

7. Overlooked mechanism: lazy per-epoch augmentation. Each epoch loop augments, interpolates and permutes all 50k images at every resolution it touches, including the final loop of about 13 steps, which wastes most of a full-dataset pass. Making this lazy keeps the math identical and could save about 1–2%; that is still the safest gain. A second candidate: Lookahead's foreach copy runs over the frozen params too. Skipping it is nearly free.

8. Transfer to the PCIe judge: absolute times should run 5–10% higher, and the lever ranking should mostly hold.

Unsure:
- whether seeds 13–32 are harder, or the gap is winner's curse;
- whether Inductor saves a bool mask or the fp16 output for ReLU;
- the size of the strided-conv loss on CIFAR-100;
- whether within-build runs are bit-identical.

forecasts.reason: The fused BN/activation kernels are bytes-bound, so the expected cut is about 2.3% (under the 3% bar). The loss is about 0.15 pp, which is inside the noise.
Removing the 31×31 conv output gives a big time cut, but losing the max-pool invariance costs about 0.7 pp. At about 0.5 s/pp that is worse than the dial.
Selection is roughly dial-equivalent, so it plus the top-up nets close to zero. The step count falls by only about 5, a 1.3% time cut, and the 3-seed noise swamps any difference.
13 more frozen steps at about 10 ms each saves about 0.13 s. The earlier anneal costs about 0.1–0.2 pp, which is dial-rate and cannot be resolved with 3 seeds.

cruxes: Can the build be made deterministic (pinned autotune/cudagraph kernels, deterministic wgrad), so that 0.1 pp effects become measurable? Without that, the 0.753 gate is a coin flip for every dial-rate trade.

How much time is spent outside the step graphs (full-dataset augment, interpolate and permute per epoch loop, including the mostly wasted final 13-step loop, plus Lookahead copies over frozen params)? If it is ≥2%, lazy identical-math pipelining beats every remaining accuracy trade.
Does the strided-conv stem lose less than ~0.4 pp on CIFAR-100? If so, its ~7% time cut plus a top-up would beat the dial and dominate the freeze levers.
